method: camera traps (Cuddeback and Browning), two sessions; independent detection records generated with a >=30-min threshold; kernel density activity of striped hyena records
conditions: Wild striped hyenas in Kappathagudda Wildlife Sanctuary, Gadag District, Karnataka, India. Session 1: 1 June to 1 July 2023, 48 stations (96 Cuddeback C1 cameras, two per station), 31 days, 1,488 trap nights; Session 2: 15 January to 16 February 2024, 121 Cuddeback and Browning cameras at 83 locations, 32 days, 2,656 trap nights. Results: in Session 1 (n = 160) activity peaked at dawn (05:00-07:00) and dusk (18:00-20:00); in Session 2 (n = 97) activity was more evenly spread through the night with a clear increase between 20:00 and midnight, so the two sessions differ in shape. Abstract: 'predominantly crepuscular and nocturnal activity'; Discussion: 'primarily nocturnal and crepuscular'. Sessions differ in survey effort (48 vs 83 stations) and season (June versus January-February). Sexes not distinguished (the Introduction says the lack of sexual dimorphism makes sexing striped hyenas challenging). The text read mentions no bait or lure.
